clue.text: Boy's description of a sort of yearbook?

definitions.meaning: a male first name, as borne by many boys

definitions.text: description of a sort of yearbook
definitions.meaning: the calendar introduced by Julius Caesar is named after him with this adjective, and a calendar is a book of the year

explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link ('Boy is description of...'). 'Yearbook' is a playful way of describing a calendar, here the one Julius Caesar introduced.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a male given name and the adjective for Caesar's old calendar system.

clue.text: 10's senior citizen, one taken for a ride

parts.note: the first name at 10 shortens to its familiar form, with the possessive s kept
OAP, old-age pensioner, is a British term for a senior citizen

explanation.surface: A writer's elderly relative turns out to be easily conned.
explanation.walkthrough: OAP (old-age pensioner) is everyday British shorthand for a retired person.
explanation.definitionFit: This British name stands for an ordinary gullible person who is easily exploited or duped.

clue.text: King-size, or possibly regal

indicators.note: possibly suggests that regal might be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: Something very big might be described as royal.
explanation.definitionFit: King-size items are extra big, a synonym for big or ample.

clue.text: Somebody else getting nothing in articles right

indicators.note: in places the zero for nothing inside the two articles

parts.note: an and the are the indefinite and definite articles
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A different person receives nothing in the paperwork, quite rightly.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun means an additional or different person, someone other than the one mentioned.

clue.text: Part of our capital in farm buildings, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word for farm buildings is spoken, giving a name of the same sound

parts.note: barns are farm buildings for storing crops or housing animals

explanation.surface: Somewhere in London resembles a collection of farm buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: BARNES is a district of south-west London, the 'capital' for this British paper.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a riverside suburb in the London borough of Richmond upon Thames.

clue.text: Help to trap bird — a loon

indicators.note: to trap means the word for help surrounds the bird, closing it in

parts.note: aid means help
the rhea is a large flightless South American bird

explanation.surface: Someone helps to catch a bird, which turns out to be a diver.
explanation.walkthrough: A loon is a diving bird, a natural pick in a clue about birds, but here it means a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Loon is informal for a silly person, a synonym for a scatterbrained fool.

clue.text: Whaling centre in North America — fishing gear catches food

indicators.note: catches means the fishing gear closes around the word for food

parts.note: a net is fishing gear
tuck is British slang for food, especially sweets eaten at school

explanation.surface: A whaling port in America where nets haul in food.
explanation.walkthrough: TUCK is British schoolchild slang for snacks and food.
explanation.definitionFit: The Massachusetts island was the world's leading whaling port in the early nineteenth century.

clue.text: Dodgy American given power in religious group

indicators.note: in places the American and power pieces inside the religious group

parts.note: a sect is a religious group
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A shady American gains influence within a cult.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodgy and the adjective both mean questionable, not to be trusted.

clue.text: Wartime heroine's bijou little poem?

definitions.meaning: ... Sansom was a British agent in occupied France during the Second World War, awarded the George Cross
a tiny ode, with the diminutive ending -ette run on, would be a little poem

explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link. The second definition is a playful coinage: ODE plus the diminutive ending -ETTE, sharing an E.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the first name of a famous SOE agent and jokingly a small ode.

clue.text: Novel about deep gloom after red card

indicators.note: after places the phrase meaning 'about deep gloom' behind the red card

parts.note: hearts are a red suit in a pack of playing cards, so a heart is a red card
of can mean about, as in 'tales of the sea'
darkness is deep gloom

explanation.surface: A footballer sent off sinks into despair after being shown the red card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red card' suggests football, but it is a playing card from the red suit of hearts.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Conrad's 1899 novella about a journey up the Congo is a famous work of fiction.

clue.text: Writer of 9 had no prose altered after his initial letters

parts.note: the writer's initials are J and C, each placed before part of the rearranged letters

indicators.note: after says the rearranged letters split so that each half follows one of the writer's initials
altered says the letters of 'had no prose' are changed into a new order

parts.note: the writer's initials are J and C, each placed before part of the rearranged letters

explanation.surface: An author who wrote nothing in prose changed after signing with his initials.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pretends an author gave up prose, but 'altered' shuffles those three words, and 'after his initial letters' makes each of his names begin with its own initial, J and C, so the C lands mid-answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Polish-born British novelist wrote the novella at 9 across.

clue.text: Novel achievement from man on baseline — not John McEnroe!

definitions.text: Novel achievement from man on baseline — not John McEnroe!

parts.words: Novel achievement from man on baseline — not John McEnroe!
parts.note: a tennis player at the baseline who stays calm, unlike the famously loud US star McEnroe, would be a hushed person from the USA; a novelist achieved a book with that title

explanation.walkthrough: John McEnroe was a notoriously noisy American tennis player who often stood on the baseline; his opposite is the title of Graham Greene's 1955 novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Graham Greene's novel set in Vietnam bears this title, which also describes a calm US tennis player.

clue.text: Poisonous plant ruining pasture (Eastern)

indicators.note: ruining means the word pasture is wrecked, its letters thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A toxic weed is spoiling the grazing land in the east.
explanation.definitionFit: The upas is a Javanese tree whose sap was used as arrow poison.

clue.text: Regular form of sweetener used in cup

definitions.text: Regular form of sweetener used in cup

parts.words: Regular form of sweetener used in cup
parts.note: a regular solid with six square faces, made of the sweet stuff stirred into a cup of tea

explanation.walkthrough: 'Regular form' sounds like the usual kind, but it is a geometric regular solid with six square faces.
explanation.definitionFit: A block of compressed sweetener shaped like a six-sided solid, dropped into tea or coffee.

clue.text: Information about end of fight in American territory

indicators.note: about means the word for information goes around the other piece

parts.note: data is information
KO, a knockout, ends a boxing fight

explanation.surface: News arrives about the conclusion of a battle in the American West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of fight' is not the last letter T but a knockout, KO.
explanation.definitionFit: Before statehood, Dakota was an organised territory of the United States.

clue.text: Veteran runs after coach

indicators.note: after puts the abbreviation for runs behind the word for coach

parts.note: a stage, or stagecoach, is a horse-drawn coach
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An old hand goes running after the team coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' looks like a trainer, but it is a stagecoach.
explanation.definitionFit: An old stager is an experienced veteran of some activity.

clue.text: The second part has to serve the first, hence delay

definitions.text: The second part has to serve the first
definitions.meaning: a lag is a convict, and convicts serve time, so the second word serves the first
a pause between cause and effect

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hence' is a link. A LAG is British slang for a convict, who must serve TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an interval or pause between one event and a related one.

clue.text: Once again, scrub about 100 on list

parts.note: re means about, as in business letters
C is the Roman numeral for 100
to list is to lean over, as a ship does

explanation.surface: Scrub the floor again, around a hundred items on a checklist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'List' looks like a roll of items, but it is a ship leaning to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrub once more is simply to wash something a second time.

clue.text: Lack of distinction in president I typically detected

indicators.note: detected says the letters are found running through the words 'president I typically'

explanation.surface: A leader is typically found to be indistinguishable from the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Identity in its sense of sameness means there is no difference between things.

clue.text: Can soldier put up with onset of enemy fire?

indicators.note: put up, in a down clue, says the can and soldier pieces are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a can is a tin
GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: onset of means the first letter of the word enemy is taken

explanation.surface: Can a soldier tolerate the start of enemy shooting?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up' turns TIN GI as one run, giving IGNIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire something is to set it alight, a synonym for kindling.

clue.text: He gets away with extremely egregious prank

indicators.note: extremely means the extremes of egregious, its first and last letters, are taken

parts.note: a caper is a prank or escapade

explanation.surface: A man flees after pulling off an outrageous stunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who gets away from captivity is a runaway or fugitive.

clue.text: Restaurant's rent low, raised

parts.note: a rent is a tear or rip

indicators.note: raised, in a down clue, says the word for low is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to low is to moo like cattle

explanation.surface: A café's rent is low but has gone up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like a payment but is a tear; 'low' is the noise cattle make, MOO, turned upward to OOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea room is a small café or restaurant serving tea and light meals.

clue.text: See 11
See 10
Player put on top of the charts

definitions.meaning: in bridge the four players are named by compass points

definitions.text: put on top of the charts
definitions.meaning: maps and charts conventionally show this compass point at the top

explanation.walkthrough: 'The charts' suggests pop music, but they are maps, which put this compass direction at the top.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a bridge seat and the direction printed at the top of a map.

clue.text: Work of author at the top, French novelist's imitator

definitions.text: Work of author at the top

parts.note: Gustave Flaubert, author of Madame Bovary, was a French novelist
a parrot is a mimic, one who imitates

explanation.surface: A famous writer's work turns out to be just an imitation of a French master.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Author at the top' is the writer whose names are the first two across entries, 1 and 4, in the top row.
explanation.definitionFit: Julian Barnes wrote the 1984 novel of this title about an amateur Flaubert scholar.

clue.text: See 26
US evangelist's naive pronouncement as author

parts.note: Billy Graham was a famous American evangelist

indicators.note: pronouncement signals that the word for naive is spoken, giving a surname of the same sound

parts.note: green means naive or inexperienced

explanation.surface: An American preacher makes a simple-minded declaration in the role of writer.
explanation.definitionFit: The English novelist wrote Brighton Rock and The Power and the Glory.
